newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end mostly higher, pork bellies mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end mostly higher, pork bellies mixed.

text.p: CME hog futures closed mostly higher, while pork bellies closed mixed.

Floor sources said the recent resiliency of hog futures had traders reluctant to aggressively sell the market. This is the second consecutive session where futures traded lower during the session only to close higher.
The December contract has closed higher for eight consecutive sessions, rising from 52.10 cents October 22 to Tuesday's 56.20.
Forecasts for higher cash pork prices later this month and futures' inability to break lower continued to attract buying, traders said.
"Nobody wants to sell this market, because they think after Thanksgiving it (pork) will get red hot," said one hog trader.

Pork bellies were pressured by weak cash prices Monday and news hog marketings Monday exceeded USDA estimates, they said. Early Tuesday USDA reported 117,000 head were actually marketed Monday in interior Iowa/southern Minnesota markets. versus the estimate of 105,000.
The larger-than-expected hog marketings Monday plus steady to weak cash pork bellies weighed on pork belly futures Tuesday.
"Cash was supposed to be higher yesterday and it actually traded steady to down a penny," said one pork belly trader.
Hogs closed down 0.125 to up 0.300 cent with December up 0.250 at 56.200. Pork bellies closed up 0.250 to down 0.125 with February 1997 off 0.075 at 69.400.
